inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: The government’s claim that it has met the “most significant demands” looks like a carefully managed attempt to make workers’ concerns disappear without giving them the legally binding job security they’re demanding. The protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike show they don’t trust official assurances—and rightly so. This feels less like a genuine resolution than a coordinated effort to control the story while leaving workers’ futures exposed.
